Resistance summary per Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate

Source: R/burigangaamr_isolates.R
burigangaamr_isolates.Rd

One row per isolate with the counts of resistant and intermediate results, the number of antibiotic classes with resistance, the antibiotics listed as nonsusceptible in supplementary table S6 and the multidrug resistance flag of that table.

Usage

burigangaamr_isolates

Format

A tibble with 50 rows and 7 variables

isolate_id

Identifier of the Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate as used in the supplement: the sampling site letter (A to G), the water sample number at that site (1 to 3) and the colony letter (a to d), for example A1a.

site

Sampling site along the Buriganga River between Sadar Ghat and Midford Ghat, coded A to G as in the supplement. The article (Table 2) describes each site by the nearby source of pollution: A plastic waste and oil spills, B ship dockyard, C household waste, D sewage water of Dhaka City, E medical waste, F chemical waste of mills and factories, G boat dockyard.

n_resistant

Number of the nine antibiotics to which the isolate is resistant, counted from the interpretations in burigangaamr.

n_intermediate

Number of the nine antibiotics with an intermediate result, counted from the interpretations in burigangaamr.

n_classes_resistant

Number of antibiotic classes (of six) with at least one resistant result, counted from burigangaamr. Equals the count reported per strain in supplementary table S6.

nonsusceptible_antibiotics

Codes of the antibiotics with a resistant or intermediate result, comma separated, as listed per strain in supplementary table S6.

multidrug_resistant

Whether supplementary table S6 flags the isolate as multidrug resistant, which the article defines as resistance to three or more antibiotic classes. TRUE for 14 isolates; the abstract and table S7 count 13, the difference being isolate B1c, which is resistant to two classes.

Source

Sharif, D. I., Amin, F., Mehbub, M. H. and Ratul, R. I. (2024). Distribution and antibiotic resistance patterns of Pseudomonas aeruginosa across different point sources of pollution in the Buriganga River, Bangladesh. Journal of Water and Health, 22(12), supplementary table S6 and counts derived from tables S3 and S4. https://doi.org/10.2166/wh.2024.270, CC BY 4.0.

Examples

head(burigangaamr_isolates)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   isolate_id site  n_resistant n_intermediate n_classes_resistant
#>   <chr>      <fct>       <int>          <int>               <int>
#> 1 A1a        A               2              1                   2
#> 2 A1b        A               2              0                   2
#> 3 A1c        A               2              1                   2
#> 4 A1d        A               3              1                   2
#> 5 A2a        A               2              0                   2
#> 6 A2b        A               1              1                   1
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: nonsusceptible_antibiotics <chr>,
#> #   multidrug_resistant <lgl>
# multidrug resistant isolates per site
table(burigangaamr_isolates$site, burigangaamr_isolates$multidrug_resistant)
#>    
#>     FALSE TRUE
#>   A     8    0
#>   B     3    1
#>   C     4    0
#>   D     4    4
#>   E     5    3
#>   F     3    5
#>   G     9    1
